L-glessner-entry-section-2228
      Cutback Prairie doorway and recessed carving
      
    
    
    Decision
    Reconstruct the entry section from native HABS IL-1015 sheet5, original Richardson office doorway23A (AIC microfilm frame29) and the owner's close-up. The lower Prairie wall slopes outward toward grade while the cutback jamb panels remain vertical; their angular outer boundaries narrow from10.7ft at5.6ft above the sill to9.1ft at the sill. The0.6ft projection at grade and short closed corner returns are bounded reconstructions, not a new footprint survey. The door keeps its5x7.75ft aperture and existing datum. A single broad threshold replaces two projecting risers; the approach/curb gap widens to9.6ft to clear it. Its visible rise is6.36in above the existing display-lifted paving. The header retains a level bearing but rises0.3ft from its shoulders to a shallow central crown; the built drawing supports this shaped edge rather than an ideal regular trapezoid. The fan spring moves down0.3ft while its radii remain. The carved field sits0.27m behind the facade, with its backing45mm farther back, and a hollow archivolt connects it to the outer fillet. Relief geometry carries that depth; colour does not stand in for recess. Individual leaves and rock fractures remain reconstructed. Approximate bounds are+/-0.15ft in elevation and+/-0.08m in depth. HABS is later surviving fabric; the original section is design intent, corroborated by the built detail, not proof of exact1904 dimensions. The modern wreath is excluded. Source pixels are not textures.
